question: Does a real LLM agent (same model/tools/budget) learning multi-parameter (path+body+headers) parameterized mechanisms on resource A succeed on never-observed resource B for EXECUTABLE binding on unseen identifiers, vs COLD vs instructions vs retrieval/RAG vs 0-token replay, measuring end-to-end tokens+browser+retrieval+verification+repair latency and amortized maintenance on WebArena-Verified v2 family hold-out (target >=10 families, 192 tasks, 49 templates, duplication 0.9479; minimum 60 tasks across 10 families if substrate constrained) — demonstrating parameterized transfer beyond the 5.42% synthetic single-param ceiling and reporting false_accept and UNKNOWN abstention?
hypothesis: A multi-parameter induction mechanism that induces distinct parameter slots per varying field (path segment, body field, header value) from 3-5 demonstrations on resource A (e.g., SKUs A1..A5, stores A) and registers one parameterized mechanism per family at confidence >=0.80 via SpiderKernel (registry + required_slots | template_slots + _bind) will resolve EXECUTABLE with correct bound_action on never-observed resource B identifiers (zero training overlap for B values) and, when executed by the same LLM agent (same model gpt-4o-mini or equivalent, same Playwright toolset, same step budget 15, same max tokens 4096, same temperature 0), achieve: (H1) success on B >=0.65 and > each baseline by >=0.12 absolute (vs B-COLD cold LLM, B-INSTR instructions, B-RAG retrieval, B-REPLAY exact replay), (H2) EXECUTABLE rate >=0.75 and binding correctness >=0.90 among EXECUTABLE, (H3) false_accept <=0.10 and UNKNOWN abstention calibrated (UNKNOWN 0.0-0.15 at low novelty, >0 only when required_slots missing or verification fails), (H4) amortized cost per success (tokens+browser+retrieval+verification+repair, distill 1000 tok amortized over f=10 added only to SPIDER) cheaper than B-COLD by >=25% and cheaper than B-RAG/B-REPLAY on held-out families, demonstrating multi-parameter transfer beyond the prior 5.42% single-param/common-prefix synthetic ceiling (EXP-PRODUCT-33528829801 audit PASS bounded to 10 single-char identifiers, EXP-PRODUCT-33741671686 harness-only multi-param 21/21 binding but not kernel).
falsifier: FALSIFIED if ANY of: (F1) SPIDER success on unseen B <0.50 or not > B-COLD by >=0.12 (Wilson 95% CI overlap) and not > B-RAG and not > B-REPLAY (i.e., no advantage over strongest memory baseline); (F2) EXECUTABLE rate <0.50 or binding correctness <0.70 (parameter induction collapses slots or leaves unsubstituted ${} templates); (F3) false_accept >0.15 or UNKNOWN miscalibrated (UNKNOWN 0.0 when should abstain leading to contamination, or UNKNOWN >0.40 on valid B with correct params); (F4) amortized cost per success SPIDER >= B-COLD (no saving) and >= B-RAG on families where RAG hits (parameterization adds no economics beyond retrieval). MIXED if F1 fails on success margin but F2 passes (mechanism binds but agent fails downstream verification/repair). MEASUREMENT_INVALID if: harness cannot induce distinct slots (slot collision), registry/resolve not exercised via real required_slots/_bind, Playwright verification broken (no postcondition check), <60 valid tasks after filtering duplication 0.9479, or LLM API unavailable for >50% of trials (distinguish from valid negative). Prior synthetic ceiling 5.42% token saving and single-param common-prefix heuristic are the null to beat.

baselines.description: Cold LLM agent with no SPIDER memory: same model/tools/budget (15 steps, Playwright browser, same prompt without retrieved mechanisms). Cost = full LLM exploration tokens + browser calls + latency per task. Upper-bound full-re-exploration cost. No retrieval, no verification shortcut, no distill. Tests whether SPIDER adds value beyond base agent.
baselines.expected: Success lower than SPIDER on held-out families; cost flat vs novelty; used as denominator for saving ratio. Expected SPIDER success >= COLD +0.12.

baselines.description: Site-specific hand-authored instructions baseline: same LLM agent supplied with natural-language site instructions (e.g., WebArena shopping procedure) but no parameterized mechanism or retrieval. Instruction tokens 200 amortized over f=10 (20 tok/task). Cost = instruction amortized + full identifier-specific steps (agent must discover B identifiers). Tests whether instructions alone achieve transfer without SPIDER param slots.
baselines.expected: Cost slightly below COLD but above SPIDER; success below SPIDER on multi-param families. SPIDER expected to beat INSTR by >=0.10 success and >=15% amortized cost.

baselines.description: Semantic retrieval / RAG over prior trajectories: same LLM agent retrieves nearest successful trajectory from training set A by Jaccard over intent+state keywords (threshold 0.30, same as pre-2.0 Graph) and replays verbatim without parameter induction. Retrieval cost 200 tok +150ms per task. If retrieved trajectory identifiers match test B at verification (exact param equality check via postconditions), reuse at 0 LLM tokens for matching prefix; otherwise fallback to COLD LLM exploration for mismatched steps. Success derived from verification outcomes. Hit/miss measured directly; family hold-out ensures many misses at B.
baselines.expected: At most 1-2 families with incidental overlap (duplication 0.9479) may hit; overall success << SPIDER because without parameterization every novel B identifier triggers fallback. SPIDER expected success >= RAG +0.12 and cost <=0.80x RAG amortized.

baselines.description: 0-token exact replay (TERX/BrowserBash) with LLM fallback: if test task's full parameterized identifier sequence exactly equals a training trajectory A (exact string equality on action_template including path+body+headers, no parameterization), replay at 0 LLM tokens + 1 verification browser call (50 tok, 90ms) +1 browser execution; otherwise replay fails verification and falls back to COLD LLM exploration for full task. Strongest exact-repeat economics baseline. Hit cost = 50 tok verification only; miss cost = COLD cost. Hit_rate measured inside compared set (expected ~0.0 on family hold-out, ~1.0 on same-family control).
baselines.expected: Hit_rate ~0.0 on held-out families (by design, B never observed) -> cost = COLD. SPIDER expected cheaper than REPLAY on held-out (SPIDER EXECUTABLE) and within 2x of REPLAY on same-resource control (where REPLAY hits at 50 tok).

baselines.description: Literal (zero-parameter) mechanism replay: distill literal mechanisms (current kernel distill) without parameter induction and attempt resolve on B via exact registry match. Tests that parameterization is necessary (literal should fail on unseen B).
baselines.expected: Success ~0.0 on held-out B (no EXECUTABLE), EXECUTABLE 0.0, confirming literal cannot handle novelty. Validates that any SPIDER success is due to param slots, not trivial match.

positive_control.description: Two positive controls exercising real pipeline: (PC1) Same-resource literal hit: training resource A mechanism replayed on same resource A with identical identifiers must achieve 100% success via B-REPLAY-TERX pipeline with 0 LLM tokens +1 browser verification call (50 tok) and measured hit_rate=1.0 on same-A holdout (5 tasks). Validates substrate can measure 0-cost case and Playwright verification works. (PC2) Multi-param regression: harness-induced mechanism from 3 A observations with path+body+headers varying (same induction as SPIDER) tested on same A via actual registry/required_slots/_bind/verify must resolve EXECUTABLE with correct bound_action (binding correctness 1.0) and success >=0.90 with reused>=0.85, confirming induction works before testing generalization to B. Both use measured verification outcomes, not forced constants.
positive_control.expected_behavior: PC1: B-REPLAY same-A cost 50 tokens, 1 browser call, success 1.0, hit_rate 1.0. PC2: multi-param same-A EXECUTABLE 1.0, binding 1.0, success >=0.90. Failure due to harness binding errors or verification broken -> MEASUREMENT_INVALID, not falsification.

null_control.description: Two null controls exercising real semantics: (NC1) Shuffled slot mapping: randomly permute learned parameter_slots -> identifier binding (e.g., swap ${sku} with ${store_id}) before SPIDER resolve on same held-out B tasks via actual registry/_bind/verify; each task incurs real retrieval+verify+fallback costs based on verification outcomes (mismatched binds fail verification and trigger repair/fallback cost, introducing variability). Expected Spearman |rho|<0.25 vs novelty and success <= B-COLD, false_accept elevated >=0.25, proving observed transfer requires correct parameterization not any reuse. (NC2) Random retrieval: SPIDER retrieval returns random registry entry instead of ranked match, UNKNOWN disabled, via actual ranking path; expected cost flat, false_accept >=0.30 or success <= B-COLD, demonstrating ranking/gating matters. Both go through actual binding/verification so they CAN fail the expected null pattern if mapping truly matters (not guaranteed flat).
null_control.expected_behavior: NC1 shuffled success <= B-COLD, false_accept >=0.25, binding correctness <0.50, |effect| small. NC2 random false_accept >=0.30 or success <= B-COLD. If NC1 shows success >= SPIDER -0.05, observed SPIDER effect is spurious (task difficulty confounded) -> measurement invalid for param-inherit claim.

measurement_validity: 1. Real LLM execution (not token proxy): same model (gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 or equivalent approved, temperature 0, seed 42 where supported) with identical Playwright toolset (navigate, click, fill, type, select, goBack, observe DOM) and identical budget (max 15 steps, max 4096 output tokens, 30s per step timeout) across SPIDER/COLD/INSTR/RAG/REPLAY. Each task cost = measured LLM input+output tokens (tiktoken or API usage), browser calls (count + wall ms), retrieval tokens/latency (200 tok+measured ms if SPIDER/RAG), verification tokens/latency (50 tok+measured ms if EXECUTABLE attempted), repair tokens/calls if verification fails (1 LLM step). Distill cost 1000 tok amortized over f=10 added ONLY to SPIDER for amortized comparison (honest accounting). No formula-from-novelty cost.

2. Family hold-out with zero B overlap: WebArena-Verified v2 census loaded from repo cache, /tmp/webarena, or verified CSV (192 tasks, 49 templates, duplication 0.9479 per portfolio). Deduplicate by template+intent hash; require >=10 families with >=3 tasks each, each family has >=2 resource pools A/B with disjoint identifiers (SKU, store, user, issue IDs). Training uses 3-5 exemplars from A only; test B values have zero exact value overlap with A for parameterized slots (verified by value set intersection =0). Family hold-out (not random split) prevents site identity leakage; hold-out families never seen during distill. Minimum 60 valid tasks (6 per family) required for decision; target 120-192 if LLM budget allows. Source, duplication handling, and family split logged in provenance.json; claim ceiling bounded to WebArena-Verified or isomorphic Flask mock if WebArena inaccessible (disclosed).

3. Multi-parameter mechanism implementation: harness-level distill_parameterized with _extract_varying_values that supports path+body+headers varying fields, distinct slot naming per field-path (e.g., body.sku -> ${sku}, headers.X-Request-ID -> ${request_id}, path segment -> ${store_id}), structure-similarity >=0.75 and field-path relevance filter (only action-template-relevant paths: url/path, body.*, headers.*). Registry stores one parameterized mechanism per family at confidence 0.90 via actual registry write/read. At resolve time, required_slots = set(parameter_slots) | template_slots present in action_template; freshness gating via behavioral_score threshold 0.25 (if available) and confidence gating <0.80 -> UNKNOWN abstention; if UNKNOWN -> fallback to COLD LLM cost for remaining steps; if EXECUTABLE -> bound_action = _bind(action_template, params) via actual _bind and Playwright execution + verification checks postconditions; on verification failure charge repair cost and count false_accept if binding wrong. No forced constants; all rates verification-derived with genuine variability. Code path must be kernel-integrated (src/spider/kernel.py or src/spider/param_induction.py) not only run_experiment.py copy, verified by audit.

4. Strong baseline execution on identical held-out set: all baselines run on same family hold-out B tasks with identical LLM/tools/budget and same verification logic. B-RAG retrieval uses Jaccard TAU=0.30 and success follows verification (retrievable only if template matches). B-REPLAY uses exact action_template string equality to decide hit/miss. B-INSTR instruction tokens correctly amortized as 200/f. B-LITERAL uses literal kernel distill without slots. No baseline handicapped by unavailable tooling; all costs measured in same units (tokens, ms, calls).

5. End-to-end cost accounting with honest amortization: per-task cost measured as above; amortized cost per success = (total_tokens + distill_tokens/f)/success_rate where distill_tokens 1000 added only to SPIDER and instruction_tokens 200 amortized as 200/f for INSTR only. Report both raw per-task and amortized (f=1,10,100) with bootstrap 5000 stratified by family for CI on cost ratios and success differences. Latency includes LLM + browser + retrieval + verification + repair. Token, browser, latency reported separately and combined (weighted).

6. Verification and calibration: verification is deterministic postcondition match (_matches) on observed DOM/state after Playwright execution (not LLM-as-judge). Verification AUROC and false_accept/false_reject measured; report verification success vs true task success correlation. UNKNOWN abstention measured per family; report ECE (expected calibration error) for confidence vs success. Freshness guard behavioral_score exercised where available (runtime distributed session if present).

7. Statistics honoring family structure: primary success comparison SPIDER vs each baseline uses McNemar or paired bootstrap stratified by family (family as block), two-sided p<0.05 with family-clustered SE; power >0.80 to detect 0.12 success delta at n>=60 per condition (power analysis n=60, alpha 0.05, baseline 0.45 -> delta 0.12 gives power 0.82). Binding correctness and EXECUTABLE rate reported with Wilson 95% CI. Cost ratio CIs via bootstrap stratified by family (5000 resamples). No degenerate 5-bin Spearman with ties; family-clustered permutation for null controls. Significance requires both primary success margin and EXECUTABLE/binding gates.

8. Prereg frozen before any outcome-bearing measurement; code, fixtures, model version, proxy constants, and decision thresholds hashed in freeze.json. Deterministic seeds (PYTHONHASHSEED=0, random.seed 42, LLM seed 42), all hashes logged. Raw evidence preserved: per-task CSV with tokens, calls, latency, success, bound_action, verification, UNKNOWN, false_accept; registry JSON with slots and templates; cost_config JSON; Playwright traces sampled.
decision_rule: SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST requires ALL of (C1)-(C6) measured via actual LLM+Playwright pipeline (not proxy): (C1) SPIDER success on held-out B M-SUCCESS-SPIDER >=0.65 and > B-COLD by >=0.12 absolute (family-stratified bootstrap 95% CI lower >0.02) and > B-RAG by >=0.12 and > B-REPLAY by >=0.12 and > B-INSTR by >=0.10; (C2) mechanism quality M-EXECUTABLE-SPIDER >=0.75 and M-BINDING-CORRECT >=0.90 (Wilson lower >=0.80) with zero unsubstituted ${} templates among EXECUTABLE; (C3) safety M-FALSE-ACCEPT-SPIDER <=0.10 and M-UNKNOWN-RATE-SPIDER in [0.00,0.15] on valid B (no excessive abstention) and B-LITERAL success <=0.15 on same B (literal fails, confirming param necessity); (C4) economics M-AMORTIZED-SAVING-SPIDER-vs-COLD >=25% cheaper at f=10 (cost per success) and SPIDER cheaper than B-RAG on held-out families (ratio <=0.85) with bootstrap CI not crossing 1.0; (C5) controls: PC1 same-A replay hit_rate 1.0 cost 50 tok success 1.0 pass and PC2 multi-param same-A EXECUTABLE 1.0 binding 1.0 success >=0.90 pass; NC1 shuffled success <= B-COLD +0.05 and false_accept >=0.25 and NC2 random false_accept >=0.30 or success <= B-COLD (NCs go through real bind/verify, not flat guarantee); (C6) freshness/abstention reported: UNKNOWN cases have confidence <0.80 or required_slots missing, ECE <=0.15. FALSIFIED if any C1-C4 fails (excluding PC/NC substrate failures which are MEASUREMENT_INVALID). MIXED if C1 success margin fails but C2 mechanism quality passes (binds correctly but agent fails downstream). MEASUREMENT_INVALID if harness cannot induce distinct slots (collision), registry/resolve not exercising real required_slots/_bind, verification broken, <60 valid tasks after dedup, or LLM API unavailable for >50% of trials (substrate failure, not scientific falsification). All thresholds frozen; single primary outcome is C1 success margin.
product_consequence_positive: If SURVIVES: C-PARAM-INHERIT advances from EXPERIMENTAL (narrow 5.42% single-param synthetic ceiling, 10 single-char identifiers, common-prefix heuristic, harness-only multi-param 21/21 but not kernel) to VALIDATED at bounded real-LLM multi-param ceiling (WebArena-Verified v2 family hold-out, path+body+headers, real Playwright verification, parameterized transfer beyond retrieval/replay). Establishes first direct measurement that multi-parameter mechanisms learned on A generalize to never-observed B with EXECUTABLE binding and quantified economics (success +0.12 vs strongest baseline, 25% amortized saving, false_accept <=0.10). Unblocks C-LLM-INHERIT (real LLM inheritance vs strong baselines gate) and C-PRODUCT-ECON (amortized economics with honest distill accounting) for scale-up to Docker full-DOM hosting; informs productization vs TERX 0-token replay dominance (SPIDER wins where replay misses). Authorizes kernel promotion of distill_parameterized with distinct slot naming to src/spider/kernel.py (promotion_ready true, pending kernel tests). No immediate SHIPPED; requires replication on production WebArena hosting and freshness guard hardening before SHIPPED.
product_consequence_negative: If FALSIFIED: C-PARAM-INHERIT remains EXPERIMENTAL at narrow synthetic ceiling (or bounded REJECTED for multi-param real-LLM setting: parameterized transfer does not beat cold/retrieval/replay on held-out families). If MIXED (binds but no success margin), mechanism binds correctly but downstream agent/verification fails -> product must investigate Playwright execution, verification, or agent prompt, not just induction. If SPIDER not beating B-RAG/B-REPLAY (where RAG/REPLAY already miss on hold-out), multi-parameter inheritance adds no economics beyond retrievable retrieval or exact replay, supporting caching-vs-generalization tension that exact replay dominates at family hold-out; Product should redirect to higher-leverage claims C-FRESHNESS (freshness guards, UNKNOWN abstention, distributed session), C-DELTA-REPAIR (localized repair on nginx HIT/SWR/SIE verified substrate per Director dependencies runtime/graph), or C-SEMANTIC-RESOLVE (calibrated resolution), and defer C-PRODUCT-ECON scale-up to full Docker. If MEASUREMENT_INVALID due to induction collision, verification broken, or LLM keys unavailable, priority is fixing distill_parameterized kernel integration (distinct slot naming per field-path) and runtime verification AUROC substrate before re-testing param-inherit economics. Negative result still high information: definitively closes real-LLM multi-param transfer at this substrate.
estimated_cost: Real LLM API calls: target 120 tasks (10 families x12) x5 conditions (SPIDER/COLD/INSTR/RAG/REPLAY) =600 agent runs +20 positive controls +120 null controls =740 runs. Each run: ~8-12 LLM calls (agent steps) x ~1500 tokens avg = ~12k-18k tokens input+output ~ $0.04-$0.08 per run at gpt-4o-mini pricing ($0.15/1M in, $0.60/1M out). Total $30-$60 at 120 tasks; at 60 tasks $15-$30. Add retrieval/verification overhead negligible. No browser hosting beyond Playwright localhost/WebArena-Verified static fixtures (no Docker required for this gate; WebArena HTML cached). Wall-clock ~60-90 min on GitHub Actions (parallel batching 4 concurrent agents). Storage: per-task CSV ~740 rows, registry JSON, cost_config, traces sampled. Fallback to synthetic Flask mock if WebArena inaccessible adds ~200 lines harness. Deterministic seeds, all hashes logged.
expected_information_gain: HIGH: First valid real-LLM test of SPIDER's core product promise after 37 total C-PARAM-INHERIT experiments with last MEASUREMENT_INVALID 0/32 tasks (no LLM keys) and prior ceiling only 5.42% single-param synthetic saving (10 identifiers) and harness-only multi-param 21/21 binding (not kernel, no agent). Either a positive (multi-param EXECUTABLE transfer beating COLD/RAG/REPLAY on never-observed B with honest end-to-end cost and false_accept <=0.10) or a valid negative (no margin vs retrieval/replay on family hold-out where duplication 0.9479 requires genuine parameterization) decisively changes product decision: (1) whether C-PARAM-INHERIT advances to VALIDATED and unblocks C-LLM-INHERIT/C-PRODUCT-ECON amortized scale-up vs premature extrapolation closure (6 failures, logistic=constant null), (2) whether multi-parameter slot induction justifies kernel promotion despite prior KERNEL-INTEGRATION-FALSIFIED/PARTIAL, (3) whether parameterized inheritance beats TERX 90ms exact-replay dominance at low-to-moderate template novelty (duplication 0.9479) and informs commercial viability. Resolves starved-claim bottleneck (0/60 recent) and tunnel flags (graph 9/10 FRESHNESS, frontier 13/15 TV) by testing highest-leverage product mechanism with strong baselines (cold/instructions/retrieval/0-token replay) and reporting UNKNOWN abstention/ECE per Director mandate.
